notes: CHT (Community Health Toolkit / Medic cht-core) is a community-health platform built on CouchDB; the OpenFn cht adaptor is a thin generic HTTP client (get/post/put/request) pointed at a CHT instance, so the whole server API is in scope. openapi.json is Medic's own published spec for CHT API 5.3.0, saved verbatim as upstream.json (OpenAPI 3.1.0, 65 paths / 86 operations / 44 schemas) with the single addition of info.x-openfn-adaptor so the file is self-identifying; nothing else differs from upstream. The spec is generated by the vendor from @openapi JSDoc in cht-core api/src/routing.js and api/src/controllers/** plus TypeScript types in shared-libs/cht-datasource, and published to the docs host — it was verified by re-running the vendor's own generator (scripts/build/generate-openapi.js) against cht-core@master, which reproduced the same 65 paths and 86 operations. 'Full' here means the vendor's complete API-server surface (/api/v1, /api/v2, /api/v3, /api/info, /api/sms). KNOWN SCOPE GAP: the CHT API server also reverse-proxies the CouchDB databases it fronts (GET/PUT/DELETE /medic/{docId}, POST /medic/_bulk_docs, POST /medic/_bulk_get, GET|POST /medic/_changes, GET|POST /medic/_all_docs, view queries, and the per-user medic-user-<name>-meta databases, plus /_session cookie auth); workflows do use those routes through the adaptor, but they are CouchDB's API, not CHT's, and Medic's spec does not describe them, so they are absent here rather than hand-added on top of a verbatim vendor spec. Other caveats: servers[0].url is the vendor's own "/" (CHT is self-hosted, so the base URL is whatever instance host the credential points at); the /api/v2/export/* endpoints return text/csv downloads and the spec declares only that content type; and the spec uses OpenAPI 3.1 constructs (const, type arrays with null, $refs into cht-datasource types) that were kept as-is.
